correctness.rationale: Unitary cyclic Fourier downsampling folds k and k+N/2 into Q_k=(1/√2)[[1,1],[exp(-τλ_k),exp(-τλ_(k+N/2))]]. Equal magnitudes force cos(2πk/N)=0, unique k=N/4 only for N≡0 mod4; at that alias equality of phases is sin(δτ)=0. Thus one deficient rank-one block exactly. Its Gram determinant e^(-2τ)sin²(δτ) and trace 1+e^(-2τ) give explicit least eigenvalue a(δ,τ), with compact convergence a/δ²→τ²/(1+e^(2τ)). A Rayleigh test bounds the global least eigenvalue by δ²τ²e^(-2τ) at all delays, preventing maximizer escape. The unique critical point solves τ=1+e^(-2τ), proving optimized asymptotic and convergence of maximizing times.

final_claim: On an even cyclic directed nearest-neighbor Markov heat semigroup, alternate-site snapshots at 0 and τ recover exactly when N=2 mod4 or N divisible by4 with nonzero drift δ and nonresonant δτ∉πZ; otherwise nullity one. For each fixed N multiple of4, optimized least Gram eigenvalue is asymptotic δ²·0.120707519697..., with universal best delay ≈1.10885755.
limitations: N even≥4, |δ|<1, τ>0, fixed N multiple of4 in limit; exactly two snapshots, normal homogeneous generator.
